    12  /-! # Semirings and rings of sets
    13  
    14  A semi-ring of sets `C` (in the sense of measure theory) is a family of sets containing `∅`,
    15  stable by intersection and such that for all `s, t ∈ C`, `t \ s` is equal to a disjoint union of
    16  finitely many sets in `C`. Note that a semi-ring of sets may not contain unions.
    17  
    18  An important example of a semi-ring of sets is intervals in `ℝ`. The intersection of two intervals
    19  is an interval (possibly empty). The union of two intervals may not be an interval.
    20  The set difference of two intervals may not be an interval, but it will be a disjoint union of
    21  two intervals.
    22  
    23  A ring of sets is a set of sets containing `∅`, stable by union, set difference and intersection.
    24  
    25  ## Main definitions
    26  
    27  * `MeasureTheory.IsSetSemiring C`: property of being a semi-ring of sets.
    28  * `MeasureTheory.IsSetSemiring.disjointOfDiff hs ht`: for `s, t` in a semi-ring `C`
    29    (with `hC : IsSetSemiring C`) with `hs : s ∈ C`, `ht : t ∈ C`, this is a `Finset` of
    30    pairwise disjoint sets such that `s \ t = ⋃₀ hC.disjointOfDiff hs ht`.
    31  * `MeasureTheory.IsSetSemiring.disjointOfDiffUnion hs hI`: for `hs : s ∈ C` and a finset
    32    `I` of sets in `C` (with `hI : ↑I ⊆ C`), this is a `Finset` of pairwise disjoint sets such that
    33    `s \ ⋃₀ I = ⋃₀ hC.disjointOfDiffUnion hs hI`.
    34  * `MeasureTheory.IsSetSemiring.disjointOfUnion hJ`: for `hJ ⊆ C`, this is a
    35    `Finset` of pairwise disjoint sets such that `⋃₀ J = ⋃₀ hC.disjointOfUnion hJ`.
    36  
    37  * `MeasureTheory.IsSetRing`: property of being a ring of sets.
    38  
    39  ## Main statements
    40  
    41  * `MeasureTheory.IsSetSemiring.exists_disjoint_finset_sdiff_eq`: the existence of the `Finset` given
    42    by the definition `IsSetSemiring.disjointOfDiffUnion` (see above).
    43  * `MeasureTheory.IsSetSemiring.disjointOfUnion_props`: In a `hC : IsSetSemiring C`,
    44    for a `J : Finset (Set α)` with `J ⊆ C`, there is
    45    for every `x in J` some `K x ⊆ C` finite, such that
    46    * `⋃ x ∈ J, K x` are pairwise disjoint and do not contain ∅,
    47    * `⋃ s ∈ K x, s ⊆ x`,
    48    * `⋃ x ∈ J, x = ⋃ x ∈ J, ⋃ s ∈ K x, s`.
    49  
    50  -/

    60  /-- A semi-ring of sets `C` is a family of sets containing `∅`, stable by intersection and such that
    61  for all `s, t ∈ C`, `s \ t` is equal to a disjoint union of finitely many sets in `C`. -/
    62  structure IsSetSemiring (C : Set (Set α)) : Prop where
    63    empty_mem : ∅ ∈ C
    64    inter_mem : ∀ s ∈ C, ∀ t ∈ C, s ∩ t ∈ C
    65    sdiff_eq_sUnion' : ∀ s ∈ C, ∀ t ∈ C,
    66      ∃ I : Finset (Set α), ↑I ⊆ C ∧ PairwiseDisjoint (I : Set (Set α)) id ∧ s \ t = ⋃₀ I
    67  
    68  /-- A ring of sets `C` is a family of sets containing `∅`, stable by union and set difference.
    69  It is then also stable by intersection (see `IsSetRing.inter_mem`). -/
    70  structure IsSetRing (C : Set (Set α)) : Prop where
    71    empty_mem : ∅ ∈ C

    73    sdiff_mem ⦃s t : Set α⦄ : s ∈ C → t ∈ C → s \ t ∈ C
